meta.label: Admin Toolkit
meta.description: Dataiku DSS administration toolkit: diagnostics, visualizations, and management tools, with multi-instance scanning across remote DSS hosts.
meta.author: Alex Kaos

params.name: sep_security
params.label: Advanced Actions
params.description: One master password covers everything: it unlocks advanced actions (delete / replace / migrate / deploy / send) in the webapp, encrypts remote-host API keys at rest, and lets the agents run headlessly.

params.name: master_password
params.label: Master password
params.description: Leave empty to keep all mutating actions permanently locked (read-only toolkit).

params.name: red_actions_secret
params.label: Legacy Advanced Actions secret (hidden)
params.description: Pre-0.4.659 hashed secret, kept declared (hidden) so DSS does not prune it on plugin update before it can be migrated into master_password.

params.name: red_actions_password
params.label: Legacy Advanced Actions password (hidden)
params.description: Pre-0.4.659 plaintext password, kept declared (hidden) so DSS does not prune it on plugin update before it can be migrated into master_password.

params.name: host_keys_password
params.label: Legacy remote host keys password (hidden)
params.description: Pre-0.4.659 plaintext password, kept declared (hidden) so DSS does not prune it on plugin update before it can be migrated into master_password.

params.name: sep_toolkit_stores
params.label: Toolkit Data Stores
params.description: One database and one storage connection cover all toolkit-owned data, including agent chat history.

params.name: toolkit_db_connection
params.label: Toolkit database (PostgreSQL)
params.description: Agents audit trail, daily-triage store, and chat history. (None) = legacy per-feature connections.

params.name: toolkit_storage_connection
params.label: Toolkit storage (managed folders)
params.description: Archive/export folders and tables saved as datasets. (None) = legacy per-feature connections.

params.name: chat_storage
params.label: Chat storage
params.description: Where agent chats persist. Remote SQL uses the Toolkit database; changes apply on the next backend restart.

params.name: chat_db_connection
params.label: Chat SQL connection (legacy override, hidden)
params.description: Superseded by 'Toolkit database' above (Remote SQL chat now stores in the toolkit database). Kept declared (hidden) so DSS does not prune an existing value; still used when Toolkit database is unset.

params.name: chat_tables_prefix
params.label: Chat tables prefix
params.description: Physical table-name prefix (lowercase letters, digits, underscores).

params.name: dbhealth_connection
params.label: RuntimeDB Connection
params.description: PostgreSQL connection for DB Health tool (typically 'runtimedb'). Select (None) to disable DB Health.

params.name: dataset_export_connection
params.label: Save Tables as Datasets — connection (legacy override, hidden)
params.description: Superseded by 'Toolkit storage' above. Kept declared (hidden) so DSS does not prune an existing value on plugin update; still used when Toolkit storage is unset.

params.name: archive_folder_connection
params.label: Archive Folders — connection (legacy override, hidden)
params.description: Superseded by 'Toolkit storage' above. Kept declared (hidden) so DSS does not prune an existing value on plugin update; still used when Toolkit storage is unset.

params.name: outreach_mail_channel
params.label: Outreach mail channel (webapp-managed)
params.description: Managed in webapp Settings; declared here (hidden) so DSS keeps the value.

params.name: agents_audit_postgres_connection
params.label: Agents Audit — connection (legacy override, hidden)
params.description: Superseded by 'Toolkit database' above. Kept declared (hidden) so DSS does not prune an existing value on plugin update; still used when Toolkit database is unset.

params.name: backend_url
params.label: Backend base URL
params.description: e.g. https://dss.example.com/web-apps-backends/PROJECT/webappId. Empty = auto-discover the webapp on the local DSS.

params.name: enable_red_actions
params.label: Master kill-switch
params.description: OFF = every agentic action refuses, regardless of per-action gates. ON by default — each action still needs its per-action gate in the webapp (Agents → Permissions) and, for DSS-side agents, the agent's own execute setting. Verify what agents propose — don't trust blindly.

params.name: host_allowlist
params.label: Host allowlist (webapp-managed)
params.description: Managed in webapp Settings; declared here (hidden) so DSS keeps the value.

params.name: verify_tls
params.label: Verify TLS (webapp-managed)
params.description: Managed in webapp Settings; declared here (hidden) so DSS keeps the value.

params.name: http_timeout_s
params.label: HTTP timeout (webapp-managed)
params.description: Managed in webapp Settings; declared here (hidden) so DSS keeps the value.

params.name: heavy_timeout_s
params.label: Heavy-scan timeout (webapp-managed)
params.description: Managed in webapp Settings; declared here (hidden) so DSS keeps the value.

params.name: default_llm_id
params.label: Default LLM (webapp-managed)
params.description: Managed in webapp Settings; declared here (hidden) so DSS keeps the value.

params.name: agent_runtime
params.label: Agent runtime (webapp-managed)
params.description: Managed in webapp Settings; declared here (hidden) so DSS keeps the value. 'dataiku' (default) relays through the Dataiku agent kernel; 'native' runs the agent loop in the webapp backend (debugging aid + automatic fallback).

params.name: triage_connection
params.label: Triage PostgreSQL connection (legacy override, hidden)
params.description: Superseded by 'Toolkit database' above (the daily-triage store lives there). Kept declared (hidden) so DSS does not prune an existing value; still used when Toolkit database is unset. (None) + no Toolkit database disables the triage loop.

params.name: triage_score_threshold
params.label: Triage score threshold (webapp-managed)
params.description: Managed in webapp Settings; declared here (hidden) so DSS keeps the value.

params.name: auto_remediate_enabled
params.label: Autonomous actions master switch (webapp-managed)
params.description: Managed in webapp Agents → Permissions; declared here (hidden) so DSS keeps the value.

params.name: auto_remediate_actions
params.label: Auto-remediate actions (LEGACY)
params.description: LEGACY — read once to seed agent_autonomous_gates (the per-action Autonomous flags in Agents → Permissions); no longer written. Declared here (hidden) so DSS keeps the value for rollback.

params.name: agent_action_gates
params.label: Agent action gates (managed)
params.description: Managed by the webapp's Agents → Permissions page — JSON {action: bool}. Read-only sensor tools default ON; every actuator action defaults OFF until enabled there. Declared here (hidden) so DSS never prunes the saved value.

params.name: agent_autonomous_gates
params.label: Agent autonomous gates (managed)
params.description: Managed by the webapp's Agents → Permissions page (the Auto column) — JSON {name: bool}. Capabilities the NIGHTLY triage agent may plan and execute without a human in the loop. Sensors default ON, actions OFF; python-run can never be autonomous. Empty = seed once from the legacy auto_remediate_actions CSV. Declared here (hidden) so DSS never prunes the saved value.

params.name: log_ai_system_prompt
params.label: AI Log Analysis System Prompt
params.description: System prompt for AI log analysis.
params.defaultValue:
You are an expert Dataiku DSS administrator and backend engineer analyzing error logs from a DSS instance's backend.log file.

IMPORTANT RULES:
- Only analyze lines with log4j level WARN, ERROR, FATAL, or SEVERE. Completely ignore INFO, DEBUG, and TRACE lines.
- For severity, use the EXACT log4j level from the log line (e.g. [WARN], [ERROR], [FATAL]). Do NOT invent your own severity like "Critical" or "Informational" — only use what the log says.
- Do NOT mention things that are working correctly or look normal. Do NOT speculate about potential issues not evidenced in the log data.
- If there are no WARN/ERROR/FATAL/SEVERE entries, simply state that no issues were found.

Before answering, think step-by-step through each error carefully. For each error pattern:
- Reason through what component, subsystem, or configuration could cause it.
- Search the web for the specific error message, Java exception, or stack trace to find known issues, Dataiku Knowledge Base articles, community posts, or release notes.
- Cross-reference with official Dataiku documentation (doc.dataiku.com) for configuration guidance, known limitations, and recommended fixes.
- Only after researching, provide your diagnosis and remediation.

Your task:
1. Identify the root cause of each distinct error or warning pattern.
2. Tag each issue with its log4j level exactly as it appears in the log (e.g. ERROR, WARN, FATAL).
3. Provide specific, actionable remediation steps, including links to relevant documentation or KB articles when available.
4. Group related errors sharing a root cause.
5. Highlight data loss risk, security issues, or service outage indicators.
6. Do not write anything about INFO level logs, only WARN and above.

Format: markdown with headings per issue (include the log4j level in the heading, e.g. "## [ERROR] FileNotFoundException in saved model lookup"), bullet points for remediation. Start with a 2-3 sentence Executive Summary.
